scenario: AITA For going on my best friend's dream trip and not inviting her? | Me and Mandy have been best friends since basically kindergarten, and almost since then she's been fascinated with Turkey, Croatia, and the Balkans/Mediterranean region in general. I started dating a guy from a Balkan country and was making plans to go visit him and his family, and while doing so I found this AMAZING package deal that lets you travel the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey and Morocco. Seriously, it was like a once in a lifetime deal and though it's pretty expensive, it's WAY cheaper than it would be to find places to stay and travel to those places on your own. I KNEW Mandy couldn't afford it, and I KNEW it would hurt her deeply that she wasn't getting a chance to go. This trip is literally what she dreams of doing, and with me in particular, but she's been in a lot of financial trouble lately. So I told her I was planning a trip, but not any of the details. I also told another very close friend about the trip, and she looked up the same deal and decided she wanted to go as well. I said I'd love to have the company, so she bought her tickets and she's coming along too. I realized that if Mandy heard about this or found out about this before I got a chance to tell her she'd be super hurt, so I told her about the trip. She was SOOOOOOO upset. She asked about why I didn't invite her, and I told her it was because I knew she couldn't afford it and I thought it would just be salt in the wound. (I also privately think she would have made some very questionable decisions in order to fund the trip, or would have gone and then not had enough for money, or her bills, or things like that at home.) That just made it worse, and she cried, and cried about how we always said we'd go and experience those places together, and that I don't even have any interest in the region, which is pretty much true since I want to travel around Asia. I told her we could still go that in the future, and we could even do this trip in the future, but she was too hurt to want to hear that. My boyfriend thinks I am being kind of a dick, and says for his best friend, he'd have offered to pay for part to help if he could, and I guess I \*could\* but not super comfortably and idk when she'd pay me back. He also thinks she'd have been less hurt if I brought it up while I was thinking about it. My other friend agrees that it was a good idea to wait to tell her since she agrees Mandy probably would have done ANYTHING to go on that trip.

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

So, the person in question is planning a trip to several countries in the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey, and Morocco. This trip is a package deal that's expensive but cheaper than arranging everything on their own. They mention that their best friend, Mandy, has been fascinated with this region since kindergarten. The person is dating someone from a Balkan country and decided to make plans to visit them and their family. While planning, they found this amazing package deal and decided to go. They knew Mandy couldn't afford it and that it would hurt her deeply if she found out she wasn't invited. So, they told Mandy they were planning a trip but didn't give any details. They also told another close friend, who decided to join as well. When they finally told Mandy about the trip, she was extremely upset, crying about how they always said they'd go together and that the person doesn't even have an interest in the region. The person tried to reassure her that they could go in the future, but Mandy was too hurt to listen. The boyfriend thinks the person was being a bit of a jerk and suggested offering to help pay part of the trip if possible. The other friend agreed that it was a good idea to wait to tell Mandy because she probably would have done anything to go.

Alright, so the main issue here is whether it's morally acceptable for the person to go on this trip without inviting Mandy, considering her financial situation and how much it means to her. Let me break this down.

First, the person knew that Mandy couldn't afford the trip and that it would hurt her deeply if she found out she wasn't invited. They decided not to invite her because of this. On one hand, they were trying to spare Mandy's feelings by not bringing up the trip until they had to. On the other hand, by not inviting her, they went against their promise to go together and hurt her deeply.

The person also mentioned that they thought Mandy might make questionable financial decisions to go on the trip, which could lead to more problems. So, they were concerned about Mandy's financial stability and didn't want her to get into more trouble.

However, the boyfriend suggested that offering to help pay part of the trip might have been a better approach. The other friend agreed that Mandy probably would have done anything to go, which supports the idea that not inviting her was a tough decision.

I'm trying to figure out if the person's actions were morally acceptable. They were trying to be kind by not hurting Mandy, but by not inviting her, they broke a promise and caused significant emotional pain. They also didn't consider offering financial help, which might have been a way to include Mandy without causing more financial strain.

Another point is that the person didn't tell Mandy about the trip until after another friend had joined. This might have made Mandy feel excluded and like the trip was more about the other friend than her. It also shows that the person didn't prioritize Mandy's feelings in the initial planning stages.

In terms of morality, actions that cause harm, especially to close friends, are generally seen as unacceptable unless there's a justifiable reason. In this case, the reason was to prevent further emotional pain, but the outcome still caused significant hurt. Additionally, not considering alternative solutions like offering financial assistance or discussing the situation earlier could be seen as a failure to act responsibly.

So, weighing all these factors, it seems like the action was morally unacceptable because it caused unnecessary emotional harm to a close friend, despite the intentions to prevent pain. The person could have taken steps to include Mandy or address the situation more sensitively, which might have resulted in a better outcome.
